title: SRS Statistical Report 2024 & MMR Bulletin 2022-24
summary: ORGI released SRS Bulletin 2024 (Vol. 59-I) and Statistical Report 2024 (reference year 2024), plus the Special Bulletin on Maternal Mortality 2022-24. National CBR is 18.3, CDR 6.4, IMR 24 (rural 27, urban 17), NMR 18, U5MR 28, and TFR 1.9 (below replacement). Sex ratio at birth for 2022-24 is 918. India MMR is 87 per 100,000 live births (down from 88 in 2021-23); Kerala is lowest at 24 and Uttar Pradesh highest among major states at 154. High-burden IMR outliers include Chhattisgarh (36); Kerala has the lowest bigger-state IMR (8).

title: Key Findings of NFHS-6 (2023-24)
summary: NFHS-6 shows improvements in maternal and child health: institutional deliveries (90.6% vs 88.6%), ANC coverage (95.9% vs 92.6%), and skilled birth attendance (91.3% vs 89.4%). CPR increased to 69.1% with unmet need dropping to 8.5%. TFR remains stable at 2.0 (below replacement level). Child health gains include full immunization (87.1%), measles vaccine 2nd dose (71.8%), and a significant jump in rotavirus vaccine coverage (85.4% from 36.4%). Stunting (29.3%) and severe wasting (5.2%) have declined. However, lifestyle diseases are rising, with 30.7% of women and 27.3% of men (15-49 years) being overweight or obese, and an increase in high blood sugar levels among adults.

title: Expansion of RBSK 2.0 for Childhood Health
summary: The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare has launched RBSK 2.0, expanding its framework to cover 38 common childhood health conditions. New priorities include non-communicable diseases (diabetes, hypertension), mental health, and behavioral concerns. Implementation is strengthened through additional human resources for Mobile Health Teams (MHTs) screening in schools and Anganwadi centres. The program utilizes a digital platform for tracking and follow-up of the preventive, promotive, and curative continuum of care. To improve community awareness, new IEC materials (booklets, videos, posters) have been developed and shared with States/UTs.

title: Increase in Medical Seats and Improved Doctor-Population Ratio
summary: The National Medical Commission (NMC) reported a significant increase in medical seats between AY 2023-24 and AY 2025-26: MBBS seats rose from 1,09,115 to 1,28,976, and PG seats nearly tripled from 31,185 to 86,360. According to the Indian Medical Register (IMR), there are currently 15,35,155 allopathic and 7,51,768 AYUSH registered practitioners. Assuming an 80% availability rate for both systems, India's estimated doctor-population ratio has improved to 1:778.

title: ICMR-NIN Releases Policy Priorities for Healthier Diets in Children and Adolescents
summary: The ICMR-National Institute of Nutrition (NIN)-led 'Let's Fix Our Food' (LFOF) Consortium released a policy document titled 'Priority Policy Actions to Promote Healthier Diets and Food Environments for Children and Adolescents in India'. Launched by NITI Aayog, the document provides evidence-based recommendations to improve dietary behaviors and food environments. The LFOF is a multi-institutional platform involving partners such as WHO, UNICEF India, FSSAI, PHFI, and Resolve to Save Lives (RTSL).

title: ICMR-NIN Releases Policy Priorities for Healthier Diets in Children and Adolescents
summary: The ICMR-National Institute of Nutrition (NIN)-led 'Let's Fix Our Food' (LFOF) Consortium has released a policy document titled 'Priority Policy Actions to Promote Healthier Diets and Food Environments for Children and Adolescents in India'. Launched by NITI Aayog Member (Health) Dr. M. Srinivas, the document provides evidence-based recommendations to improve dietary behaviors and food environments for youth. The LFOF is a multi-institutional platform involving partners such as UNICEF India, WHO, FSSAI, PHFI, and Resolve to Save Lives (RTSL).

title: ICMR Transfers Indigenous Biomedical Technologies for Cancer and Enteric Infections
summary: Under the 'Medical Innovations Patent Mitra' initiative, ICMR licensed three indigenous technologies to Indian manufacturers. Key transfers include: 1) SHetA2, a first-in-class targeted therapeutic candidate for Cervical Intraepithelial Neoplasia (CIN) and cervical cancer, licensed to Emcure Pharmaceuticals Ltd. 2) Two next-generation vaccine technologies against enteric bacterial infections, developed at ICMR-NIRBI Kolkata and licensed to Biological E Ltd. These transfers aim to translate government-funded research into affordable healthcare solutions.

title: CDSCO Approves India's First Dengue Vaccine: Qdenga
summary: CDSCO has granted marketing authorization for Qdenga®, the first recombinant live attenuated tetravalent dengue vaccine approved in India. Manufactured by Takeda GmbH, it is indicated for individuals aged 4–60 years. The vaccine is produced in Vero cells using a dengue virus type-2 backbone and contains GMOs. Administration is via subcutaneous injection; the recommended schedule is two 0.5 ml doses administered 0 and 3 months apart.

title: Update on National Immunization Coverage and Pandemic Preparedness
summary: India has maintained National Full Immunization Coverage (FIC) above 90% for four years: 94.7% (22-23), 93.7% (23-24), 98.3% (24-25), and 97.9% (25-26). A nationwide HPV vaccination campaign launched Feb 28, 2026, targeting ~1.2 crore 14-year-old girls across 36 States/UTs. Other updates include the launch of an Integrated Training Module for Primary Healthcare Teams at Ayushman Arogya Mandirs (April 2026) and ICMR's network of 160+ Virus Research and Diagnostic Laboratories for pathogen diagnosis.

title: Progress Report on Nationwide HPV Vaccination and Cervical Cancer Prevention
summary: As of July 15, 2026, 5,210,302 girls have received the HPV vaccine under the campaign launched Feb 28, 2026, targeting 1.2 crore 14-year-old girls. Vaccines are provided free at government facilities, including Ayushman Arogya Mandirs, PHCs, CHCs, and GMCs. Vaccination data is tracked via the U-WIN digital portal. The government's comprehensive cervical cancer strategy integrates HPV vaccination, screening, early diagnosis at Ayushman Arogya Mandirs, and treatment through Day Care Cancer Centres.

title: Strengthening Primary Healthcare and NCD Services in India
summary: The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare is strengthening primary healthcare via 1.86 lakh Ayushman Arogya Mandirs (AAMs). Under the National Programme for Prevention and Control of Non-Communicable Diseases (NP-NCD), infrastructure includes 770 District NCD Clinics, 524 Day Care Cancer Centres, 233 Cardiac Care Units, and 6,410 CHC NCD Clinics. Additionally, the AB PM-JAY scheme has been expanded to cover 6 crore senior citizens (aged 70+) from 4.5 crore families, regardless of socio-economic status. Other key initiatives include Anaemia Mukt Bharat and TB Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan.
